data.gender_notes: Mus'Ab is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A companion or friend, one who is close to the heart. Mus'ab is also the name of a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The name Mus'Ab carries the meaning “Companion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mus'Ab usually hope their child will grow to embody companion and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A loyal companion on the path to righteousness.
data.etymology: Mus'Ab belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Companion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mus'Ab total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Mus'ab holds a special place in Islamic history as it was the name of one of the greatest companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Mus'ab ibn Umair al-Khadri was a young man from the Ansar (helpers) of Medina. He was an expert in Arabic poetry and was given the title "Al-Khaidrib," meaning the weary one, due to his sensitivity to the suffering of others. He was notably respected and admired by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for his bravery, dedication, and beautiful character. Mus'ab played a crucial role in the submission of the people of Khaybar to Islam, and it is a remarkable event that marks his commitment to Islam and serving the Prophet and the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: Mus'ab, as a name, holds a deep spiritual significance as it refers to the idea of companionship and friendship. In Islamic traditions, companionship refers to being in loving proximity and connection with Allah (God). The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) encouraged Muslims to seek companionship with the righteous and virtuous, as this was a means of nearness to Allah, and protected one from inner and outer adversities. By naming a child Mus'ab, parents imbue the child with a sense of the importance of true companionship with Allah and with others, and the reverence for the companionship of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) himself. The name Mus'ab can be a reminder for us all to strive for a deep, meaningful connection with Allah (God) and to cultivate virtuous friendships, thus enriching our spiritual lives and our relationship with the divine.
